outcome: Nothing since 26 January 2024 settles or moves density of hyperbolicity for complex quadratic polynomials, which every source I read still treats as open as of 11 October 2026; the in-window events bearing on it are a June 2026 MLC result for one class of infinitely renormalizable parameters that says nothing about density, a Lean formalisation of MLC conditional on two axioms, and unrelated 2026 papers the searches surfaced.
problem_asks: (1) The family: maps of the complex plane to itself that are quadratic. Read as the complex quadratic polynomials f_c(z) = z² + c with c in ℂ (every quadratic polynomial is affinely conjugate to one of these). The bullet does not say whether 'quadratic family' means these polynomials or all degree-2 rational maps; the literature on this conjecture (density of hyperbolicity, MLC) uses the polynomial reading, and I have recorded results on that basis, with rational-map analogues marked as analogues. (2) Hyperbolic: every critical orbit of f_c converges to an attracting cycle (for polynomials, the critical orbit lies in an attracting basin, with no neutral cycle). (3) The set of parameters c for which f_c is hyperbolic is open in ℂ. The sources treat openness as classical (structural stability; Mañé–Sad–Sullivan), so this part is not the open content. (4) That set is dense in ℂ. The sources give the equivalent form: every component of ℂ minus the boundary of the Mandelbrot set M is hyperbolic. The statement asks for open and dense together, for complex parameters, and makes no reality or degree restriction beyond quadratic.

events.what_happened: Grzegorz Świątek, 'Hyperbolicity is dense in the real quadratic family', arXiv math/9207219 (Stony Brook IMS preprint 1992/10). Abstract: for non-hyperbolic real quadratic polynomials, topological and quasisymmetric conjugacy classes coincide; by quasiconformal rigidity each class has one representative in the quadratic family, 'which proves that hyperbolic maps are dense'. Restricted to real parameters.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only, 6 Jul 1992. A search excerpt reports a Stony Brook revision dated March 1994; not checked.
events.delivers: Density of hyperbolic parameters in the REAL quadratic family x ↦ ax(1−x), 0 < a ≤ 4. Real parameters only; says nothing about complex c.
events.remains: Density for complex parameters c in z² + c, which is the whole of the bullet's content for complex c.

checked_by.qualification: Authors of the Annals paper and monograph on the real Fatou conjecture; experts in the field
checked_by.what_they_did: Published an independent proof of density of hyperbolicity for the real family (Annals 1997; book 1998)

events.direction: Affirmative for the real family: density holds there. Does not cut against the complex statement.

events.what_happened: Jacek Graczyk and Grzegorz Świątek, 'Generic hyperbolicity in the logistic family', Annals of Mathematics 146 (1997), pp. 1–52 (one bibliography gives 1–56). Monograph 'The Real Fatou Conjecture', Annals of Math. Studies 144, Princeton University Press, 1998. Proves that hyperbolic parameters are open and dense in the real logistic family. Secondary sources (Kozlovski–van Strien 2009 exposition; Dudko 2025 survey, ref. [22]) cite it as the real case.
events.revisions: Journal year only. The date of the first public written argument (an earlier preprint, if any) was not established, so the month and day are left out.
events.delivers: Openness and density of hyperbolic parameters in the REAL logistic family. Real parameters only.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record and academic press; authors are the proving experts
checked_by.what_they_did: Published after refereeing; the monograph gives a self-contained version of the argument

events.direction: Affirmative for the real family. Does not cut against the complex statement.

events.what_happened: Mikhail Lyubich, 'Dynamics of quadratic polynomials, I: Combinatorics and geometry of the Yoccoz puzzle', arXiv math/9503215, first submitted 1 Mar 1995. Published with Part II as Acta Math. 178 (1997), 185–247 and 247–297 (journal reference from search metadata). The arXiv abstract concerns the Yoccoz puzzle and the principal nest of annuli, with complex a priori bounds and local connectivity of J for many infinitely renormalizable quadratics as corollaries. It does not state density of hyperbolicity. Secondary sources (Kozlovski–van Strien 2009 exposition; search excerpts) credit Lyubich with the independent real-quadratic density result; I did not find that result in the Part I abstract.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only. Acta Math. 178 (1997) is the journal version.
events.delivers: Part I, as far as the abstract shows: combinatorics and geometry of the Yoccoz puzzle; complex a priori bounds and local connectivity for many infinitely renormalizable quadratics. No density statement in the abstract. Attribution of the real density result to Lyubich rests on secondary sources, not on this text.
events.remains: Density of hyperbolic parameters in the complex quadratic family. The infinitely renormalizable class covered by the a priori bounds does not by itself give density there.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the two-part paper in 1997 (journal reference from search metadata; not opened)

events.direction: Partial and not density: complex a priori bounds and local connectivity for a class of infinitely renormalizable parameters. Does not cut against the statement.

events.what_happened: Oleg Kozlovski, Weixiao Shen and Sebastian van Strien, 'Density of hyperbolicity in dimension one', Annals of Mathematics 166 (2007), 145–182, DOI 10.4007/annals.2007.166.145. A 2009 exposition by Kozlovski and van Strien cites the preprint as 2003, alongside 'Rigidity for real polynomials' (also 2003). Per a 2019 summary by Yan Gao, the result covers real one-dimensional maps: real polynomials with all critical points real, and interval and circle maps. The arXiv record was not located.
events.revisions: Preprint year from a secondary citation, not checked against the preprint itself.
events.delivers: Density of hyperbolicity for REAL one-dimensional maps, including real polynomials with all critical points real. Real only.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; authors are experts in one-dimensional dynamics
checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2007; a 2009 exposition by two of the authors restates the results

events.direction: Affirmative for the real one-dimensional family. Does not cut against the complex statement.

events.what_happened: Yongcheng Yin and Yu Zhai, 'No invariant line fields on Cantor Julia sets', arXiv math/0609255, first submitted 9 Sep 2006; v2 12 Sep 2006; v3 12 Sep 2006 (current). Abstract: a rational map with a Cantor Julia set carries no invariant line field on its Julia set. Consequence stated: a structurally stable rational map with a Cantor Julia set is hyperbolic. Journal version reported as Forum Mathematicum (2010) in a search excerpt; not checked.
events.revisions: v1 9 Sep 2006; v2 12 Sep 2006; v3 12 Sep 2006 (current).
events.delivers: For RATIONAL maps of degree d ≥ 2 whose Julia set is a Cantor set: no invariant line field, so structurally stable implies hyperbolic. Restricted to Cantor-Julia-set maps in the rational family. For the quadratic family, Cantor Julia sets occur for c outside M, where f_c is already hyperbolic (my inference from standard facts, not stated in the paper), so the result does not reach any non-hyperbolic quadratic parameter.
events.remains: Every quadratic parameter with a connected Julia set, which includes all non-hyperbolic parameters in M.

checked_by.who: Forum Mathematicum (journal), per a search excerpt
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (reported in a search excerpt; not verified on the journal page)

events.direction: Analogue (rational maps, Cantor Julia sets). Affirmative in its restricted class, and does not cut against the statement.

events.what_happened: Oleg Kozlovski and Sebastian van Strien, 'Local connectivity and quasi-conformal rigidity of non-renormalizable polynomials', arXiv math/0609710, first submitted 26 Sep 2006; v3 29 Jul 2009 (current). Abstract (opened): topologically conjugate non-renormalizable polynomials are quasiconformally conjugate; from this 'each such polynomial can be approximated by a hyperbolic polynomial'. The local-connectivity corollary (Branner–Hubbard) concerns non-renormalizable polynomials with only hyperbolic periodic points. Journal: Proc. London Math. Soc. 99 (2009), 275–296 (search excerpt, Warwick repository).
events.revisions: v1 26 Sep 2006; v2 26 Sep 2006; v3 29 Jul 2009 (current).
events.delivers: For complex polynomials of degree d ≥ 2 that are NON-RENORMALIZABLE, each is approximable by hyperbolic polynomials of the same degree. For degree 2 that is density of hyperbolicity within the non-renormalizable quadratic parameters. Hypothesis unresolved: the abstract's approximation claim has no explicit periodic-point condition, but the 2025 Timoner Vaquer thesis states it for polynomials 'without neutral periodic points'. Whether neutral cycles are excluded decides whether non-renormalizable quadratic parameters with neutral cycles are covered.
events.remains: Every renormalizable quadratic parameter, including the infinitely renormalizable ones that Levin–Przytycki name as the obstacle; and, if the neutral-periodic-point hypothesis applies, non-renormalizable parameters with neutral cycles.

checked_by.what_they_did: Reproduced, clarified and checked the Kozlovski–van Strien theorem in a 2025 master's thesis, digested in Reports@SCM 10(1) (2025)

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (journal)

events.doubts: The periodic-point hypothesis differs between the arXiv abstract (no explicit condition on the approximation claim) and the thesis summary ('without neutral periodic points'). I did not read the proof, so I cannot say which is correct.
events.direction: Affirmative for the non-renormalizable class of complex polynomials, including non-renormalizable quadratics if the hypothesis is as the abstract states. Does not cut against the statement.

events.what_happened: Wenjuan Peng, Yongcheng Yin and Yu Zhai, 'Density of hyperbolicity for rational maps with Cantor Julia sets', Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems (published online September 2011, per the Cambridge listing in a search result). Abstract (search excerpt): by quasiconformal surgery, each non-hyperbolic rational map with a Cantor Julia set can be approximated by hyperbolic rational maps with Cantor Julia sets of the same degree. No arXiv version located.
events.revisions: Journal year only. The first public written argument was not located.
events.delivers: Density of hyperbolic maps among RATIONAL maps of degree d with Cantor Julia sets. Analogue, restricted to the Cantor class. For quadratic polynomials this adds nothing to non-hyperbolic parameters (my inference, per the Cantor-set argument above).
events.remains: Quadratic polynomials and rational maps whose Julia sets are not Cantor sets.
events.direction: Analogue (rational maps, Cantor Julia sets). Affirmative in its restricted class, and does not cut against the statement.

events.what_happened: Genadi Levin and Feliks Przytycki, 'No hyperbolic sets in J∞ for infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomials', arXiv 2107.11962. v1 26 Jul 2021; v2 20 Jun 2022 (the 'final version', extended, with a corollary added and the title changed). Journal: Israel J. Math. 251 (2022), 635–656 (search excerpt). Abstract (opened): for an infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial, J∞ (intersection of forward orbits of the small Julia sets of its simple renormalizations) contains no hyperbolic sets. Introduction (opened, HTML): 'The DHC ... is widely open for the quadratic family'; 'After a breakthrough work of Yoccoz on the MLC, the only obstacle for proving DHC for quadratic polynomials are so-called infinitely renormalizable ones, see [28].'
events.delivers: A statement about the invariant set J∞ inside the Julia sets of infinitely renormalizable quadratics: no hyperbolic sets there. It does not establish density of hyperbolic parameters. The introduction's claim that infinitely renormalizable parameters are the only obstacle to DHC for quadratics is the authors' statement, not a result of this paper; it locates the obstacle and does not remove it.
events.remains: Density of hyperbolic parameters, notably among infinitely renormalizable quadratics.

checked_by.where: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11962 (arXiv record opened; journal reference from search)

events.direction: Neither settles nor cuts against density: an invariant-set result for the infinitely renormalizable class, with the authors' statement that this class is the obstacle.

events.what_happened: Dzmitry Dudko and Mikhail Lyubich, 'MLC at Feigenbaum points', arXiv 2309.02107. v1 5 Sep 2023; v2 4 Dec 2023; v3 29 Dec 2025 (current). Abstract (opened, partial): a priori bounds for Feigenbaum quadratic polynomials (infinitely renormalizable, bounded type), giving local connectivity of J and MLC at the corresponding parameters; MLC was open for the classical period-doubling Feigenbaum parameter and for complex tripling renormalizations. Journal: Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS, online first 2026 (search result; not opened).
events.revisions: v1 5 Sep 2023; v2 4 Dec 2023; v3 29 Dec 2025 (current).
events.delivers: MLC (local connectivity of M) at the Feigenbaum parameters, one special class of infinitely renormalizable parameters. The abstract does not mention density of hyperbolicity. A search excerpt attributes to the paper a remark that MLC would imply the Fatou conjecture; I did not confirm that in the text.
events.remains: Density of hyperbolicity for the quadratic family, and MLC at every other parameter.

events.what_happened: Magnus Aspenberg, Mats Bylund and Weiwei Cui, 'Slowly recurrent Collet–Eckmann maps with non-empty Fatou set', arXiv 2207.14046, v1 28 Jul 2022. Journal: Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 128 (2024), e12574 (journal reference on the arXiv page). Claim (opened): for rational Collet–Eckmann maps with slow recurrence and Julia set not the whole sphere, such maps are Lebesgue density points of hyperbolic maps, within a family with fixed critical orders and, if all critical points are simple, within the full space of rational maps of degree d ≥ 2.
events.revisions: v1 only. The journal version (2024) is inside the window, but the first public argument is the 2022 preprint.
events.delivers: A measure-density statement (Lebesgue density) about hyperbolic maps in the space of RATIONAL maps of degree d ≥ 2, for a restricted class of slowly recurrent Collet–Eckmann maps. Not the quadratic family, and not topological density.
events.remains: Density of hyperbolic parameters in the quadratic family, and maps outside the stated class.

events.what_happened: Magnus Aspenberg, Mats Bylund and Weiwei Cui, 'Collet–Eckmann maps in the unicritical family', arXiv 2402.19256. v1 submitted 29 Feb 2024 (inside the window); v2 revised 22 Dec 2025. Claim (opened): Collet–Eckmann parameters in the unicritical family are Lebesgue density points of the complement of the Mandelbrot set (the page's parenthetical identifies this as the connectedness locus). The page does not mention hyperbolicity.
events.delivers: A Lebesgue-density statement about Collet–Eckmann parameters relative to the complement of M. The complement of M is the escape region, where parameters are already hyperbolic (my inference from standard facts). So it is not a statement that hyperbolic parameters are dense inside M, and it does not reach the non-hyperbolic parameters that the bullet concerns.
events.remains: All density of hyperbolic parameters inside M, which is the bullet's content.
events.direction: Neither. A measure-density statement on a region that is already hyperbolic, so it does not bear on the bullet's density claim inside M. Recorded because it is in-window and in the same family.

events.remains: Complex parameters, and the topological density question for the complex family.

Abstract (opened): on the boundary of the central hyperbolic component H_d of degree-d polynomial space (d ≥ 3); proves local connectivity of Julia sets and a rigidity theorem on the regular part of the boundary, using Fatou trees and puzzles.

events.what_happened: Dzmitry Dudko, 'On the MLC Conjecture and the Renormalization Theory in Complex Dynamics', arXiv 2512.24171, single version, 30 Dec 2025. Abstract (opened): an expository note on recent developments in renormalization theory of quadratic polynomials with emphasis on MLC and its geometric counterparts; 'to appear in the Proceedings of the ICM 2026'. Partial full text (opened, truncated): calls MLC the central question (also the 'Rigidity Conjecture'); lists open Problem 4.3 (pseudo-Siegel a priori bounds in the remaining unbounded satellite ql cases) and Problem 4.4 (a virtual molecule version of the near-degenerate regime); acknowledgements thank Lyubich, Luo and Drach. Cites Kozlovski–Shen–van Strien [31] and Graczyk–Świątek [22] on density. Does not claim a new DHC result.
events.delivers: No new result on density of hyperbolicity. An expository status report on MLC and renormalization. The text I read did not state the DHC status for quadratic polynomials; the abstract does not mention it.
events.direction: None (expository).

Reviews standard tools (puzzles, quasiconformal conjugacies, Böttcher coordinates, holomorphic motions, complex box mappings) and reproduces, clarifies and checks the Kozlovski–van Strien theorem for non-renormalisable polynomials without neutral periodic points. Digest: Timoner Vaquer, Reports@SCM 10(1) (Catalan, 'Densitat d'hiperbolicitat en famílies de funcions racionals complexes'), 91–92, published 4 Dec 2025 (search excerpt; PDF not readable via fetch).

events.delivers: A reproduction of the Kozlovski–van Strien theorem. The abstract claims no new theorem; extension to Newton and McMullen maps is sketched as future work.

events.what_happened: Kirill Kondrashov, GitHub repository 'kirill-kondrashov/mlc' ('Mandelbrot local connectivity hypothesis'), a Lean 4 formalisation. Root theorem MLC.mlc_conjecture : LocallyConnectedSpace MLC.mandelbrotSet, which the README calls sorry-free. It depends on two project-level axioms: MLC.green_sublevel_translate_inter_mandelbrot_connected_straddling, and MLC.residualOpenVirtualNearMoleculeAxiom, which the README describes as the root-facing conjunction of Dudko–Lyubich Problems 4.3 and 4.4. The README calls the result 'a compact Lean 4 formalization of the Mandelbrot local-connectivity conjecture, conditional on two explicit mathematical inputs'. Page shows 154 commits and a 2026 copyright footer, but no commit date (opened).
events.revisions: Repository with 154 commits; no first-commit date visible. The 2026 date rests only on the footer copyright year.
events.delivers: A machine-checked reduction of MLC to two stated axioms, one of which encodes Dudko–Lyubich open problems 4.3 and 4.4 as an assumption. It does not prove MLC unconditionally, and the README does not address density of hyperbolicity.
events.remains: MLC itself, which is unproven here; density of hyperbolicity, which is not addressed.

machine_checked.axioms: Two custom project axioms, as listed in what_happened; the root theorem is sorry-free only relative to them

events.doubts: The root theorem is sorry-free only relative to two custom axioms, and one of them encodes open problems (Dudko–Lyubich 4.3 and 4.4). The README calls it conditional. I read the README only, not the Lean source, so I have not checked the axiom statements.
events.direction: None on density: a conditional formalisation of MLC, which would imply density if MLC held (a standard implication, not established in this repository).

events.what_happened: Jeremy Kahn, Alex Kapiamba and Mikhail Lyubich, 'MLC for parabolically bounded primitive renormalization', arXiv 2606.27272 (math.DS, 73 pages), single version v1 submitted 25 Jun 2026 (opened abstract and partial HTML). Abstract: a priori bounds and MLC for a class of infinitely renormalizable parameters whose renormalization type is primitive but which can approach the cusp of M; tools: Thin-Thick Decomposition, Value Calculus, Wanderers Theorem, Wave Lemma. Theorem A (HTML excerpt): every parabolically bounded family of prime primitive types has bounded a priori bounds. Theorem C: such families are rigid. 'Parabolically bounded' is defined as a finite union of types and parabolic tails. A 2025 talk by Kapiamba (CNRS, June 2025) on near-parabolic primitive combinatorics precedes this write-up, and is dated to it per the rule in §5.1.
events.delivers: A priori bounds, rigidity and MLC for infinitely renormalizable parameters of 'parabolically bounded' primitive type, a subclass of the infinitely renormalizable parameters. The abstract does not mention density of hyperbolicity or the Fatou conjecture.
events.remains: Density of hyperbolic parameters for the whole quadratic family, MLC for infinitely renormalizable parameters outside this class, and the remaining satellite and unbounded cases (Dudko's Problems 4.3 and 4.4).
events.doubts: Single unrefereed version, 73 pages. I read the abstract and part of the HTML text (truncated; references and the later sections were not read). Its claims rest on earlier Kahn–Lyubich and Dudko–Lyubich results whose status I did not check.
events.direction: Neither. Progress on MLC for a subclass of infinitely renormalizable parameters, with no stated consequence for density. It does not cut against the statement.

events.what_happened: Weiyuan Qiu and Lingrui Wang, 'Hyperbolic components of cosine family with a fixed critical point', arXiv 2603.10554 (math.CV), single version, 11 Mar 2026 (opened abstract). Results: hyperbolic components in the cosine family with a fixed critical point are of types A, C and D; all are bounded and simply connected except the type-A component; their boundaries are Jordan curves (para-puzzle method); type-C components are quasidisks.
events.delivers: Structure of hyperbolic components in the COSINE family with a fixed critical point. Not quadratic polynomials and not density.
events.direction: Not bearing on the bullet: a different family, surfaced by a density search.

events.what_happened: Igors Gorbovickis, 'Independence of multipliers via degenerations of rational maps', arXiv 2609.06200 (math.DS, cross-listed math.CV), single version, submitted 5 Sep 2026 (opened abstract). Claims: for every degree d ≥ 2, the multipliers of any 2d−2 distinct periodic orbits of a degree-d rational map are algebraically independent over ℂ, provided at most d of the orbits are fixed points; the condition is sharp by the Holomorphic Index Formula. No acknowledgement of AI or computer tools.
events.delivers: Algebraic independence of periodic-orbit multipliers in the space of rational maps. The abstract does not mention hyperbolicity density, the Fatou conjecture, or quadratic polynomials.
events.direction: Not bearing on the bullet as far as the abstract shows. Multipliers are related to hyperbolicity, but I found no link asserted in the abstract.

summary: Searched 42 queries (verbatim in search.queries), eight of them AI-specific, and opened about two dozen pages. Every source I read treats density of hyperbolicity for complex quadratic polynomials as open as of 11 October 2026. The most recent substantive status statement is Dudko's ICM 2026 expository note (arXiv 2512.24171, 30 Dec 2025), which gives no new DHC result; the most recent in-window preprint on the chain, Kahn–Kapiamba–Lyubich (arXiv 2606.27272, 25 Jun 2026), proves a priori bounds and MLC for a subclass of infinitely renormalizable parameters ('parabolically bounded' primitive type) and does not mention density. The settled cases are restrictions. Real parameters: Świątek (1992), Graczyk–Świątek (Annals 1997), and Lyubich (attribution from secondary sources; the Part I abstract does not state it). Non-renormalizable complex polynomials: Kozlovski–van Strien (arXiv 2006, reproduced in a 2025 master's thesis). That result's hypothesis is unresolved: the arXiv abstract states the approximation claim with no periodic-point condition, while the thesis states it 'without neutral periodic points'. Two close calls. (i) Levin–Przytycki's introduction says infinitely renormalizable parameters are the only obstacle to DHC for quadratics; if that is accurate, the remaining content is that class, and KKL covers only a subclass of it. Partial MLC on a class does not obviously give density on that class, and the chain MLC ⇒ DHC is the classical implication, which no source here proves in the other direction. (ii) Whether KvS covers non-renormalizable quadratics with neutral cycles. The rational-map analogues (Yin–Zhai 2006; Peng–Yin–Zhai 2011; Aspenberg–Bylund–Cui 2022) are restricted to Cantor Julia sets or slowly recurrent Collet–Eckmann maps, and I have recorded them as analogues. In-window items that are not about density: Aspenberg–Bylund–Cui (arXiv 2402.19256, 29 Feb 2024), a Lebesgue-density statement about the complement of M, which is already hyperbolic; the Lean repository (kirill-kondrashov/mlc), a conditional formalisation of MLC that depends on two custom axioms, one encoding open problems; and the Qiu–Wang (cosine family) and Gorbovickis (multipliers) papers. AI: no source I read names an AI system for this problem, and no AI system is credited with any part of it. The AI-related items found in these searches concern other problems: an OpenAI internal model's unit-distance disproof (May 2026), GPT-5.5 Pro's sum-product disproof (arXiv 2607.20525), and the Kummer–Netzer generalized Lax result (arXiv 2609.24542). I did not open 2607.20525 or 2609.24542. The Wikipedia lead (fetched) states the quadratic version, gives no status, cites only the Graczyk–Świątek book, and was last edited 28 April 2024 according to the fetched page. The 2024 Lean/MLC search aggregator and emergentmind pages were checked and were not relevant.
competing_reading: One could read the 2026 Kahn–Kapiamba–Lyubich MLC result, together with Levin–Przytycki's statement that infinitely renormalizable parameters are the only obstacle to DHC for quadratics and the Kozlovski–van Strien non-renormalizable theorem, as nearly closing DHC for the quadratic family, so that the problem would count as largely settled for its non-renormalizable part and as close to settled overall. The reply from the sources: the reduction is the authors' statement and not a theorem; Kozlovski–van Strien may exclude neutral cycles; and KKL covers only a parabolically bounded subclass of infinitely renormalizable parameters, not all of them. Density needs every parameter in the family, so these do not settle it. A second, weaker reading: the 1992–1997 real results and the Kozlovski–van Strien 2006 result show density in every case except the one the bullet asks about, so the complex problem is a single hard remainder. The sources support that description, but they do not show the remainder is small.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The full text of arXiv 2606.27272: its definition of 'parabolically bounded', its main theorems, its references, and any corollary about hyperbolicity. (b) The full text of Levin–Przytycki arXiv 2107.11962, and the reference cited as [28] in their introduction, to check the 'only obstacle' claim. (c) The exact hypotheses of Kozlovski–van Strien (arXiv math/0609710): whether 'neutral periodic points' are excluded. (d) The arXiv math.DS listings after 11 October 2026 for density-of-hyperbolicity or MLC preprints, including the Drach–Dudko work on transcendental maps (a 2026 talk abstract, not located on arXiv). (e) The Kondrashov Lean source: the statements of the two axioms, and the commit history. (f) The full text of Dudko's 2025 survey, to read its status statement for density of hyperbolicity.

events.credibility_reason: Sorry-free only relative to two custom axioms, one encoding open Dudko–Lyubich problems; axiom statements unread; conditional on MLC and silent on density.

judgement.why: The statement asks for open-dense hyperbolicity in the complex quadratic family. The real-parameter results (Świątek, Graczyk–Świątek, KSS) and Kozlovski–van Strien on non-renormalizable parameters settle restrictions of that question, so they are cases, all before the snapshot. Rational-map analogues, measure statements and other families are variants. MLC results on subclasses (Feigenbaum, parabolically bounded primitive) are scored none, not case: MLC on a class is not density on that class, and the record shows no density corollary. None of the in-window events settles or bounds density. The Kondrashov Lean repository is a conditional reduction of MLC, so none; its 2026 year date is after the snapshot. No AI is involved in any event.
judgement.doubts: Whether real-parameter density counts as a restriction (case) or a changed question (variant) is a close call. It affects only pre-snapshot rows, which are not resolved either way. The KvS neutral-cycle hypothesis is unresolved. The KKL full text was only partly read.
